learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the cutting edge of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering, whose object, in accordance with the acquired knowledge as established in section 5 of order CIN/351/2009, is the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Legislation and legal processing of projects.
Industrial sectors within the scope of the degree.
Regulations and legislation within the scope of the degree.
Ergonomics, quality, industrial heritage and transversal topics in industrial projects
teaching_methods: Information and knowledge transmission primarily through the Virtual Course
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by an in-person exam and continuous assessment activities (PEC). The exam's weight ranges from 60% to 90% depending on the student's completion of PECs. Obligatory PECs contribute 10% to the final grade, and an optional voluntary PEC can contribute an additional 30%. A minimum score of 4 out of 10 in the exam is required to sum the PEC grades. The minimum weighted final grade to pass the course is 5 out of 10.
